ExtractedNode-Input.description:
A single node in the extracted workflow tree.

The same shape covers leaf agents (`LlmAgent`, `HITLAgent`) and wrapper
agents (`SequentialAgent`, `ParallelAgent`, `LoopAgent`). `kind` says
which one. Wrapper-only and leaf-only fields stay at their defaults
when they don't apply.

Tree position is the only structural information: a node is a child of
whichever node holds it in `sub_agents`. There is no `parent_wrapper`,
no `step`, no `dependencies` — siblings in a `SequentialAgent` run in
list order, siblings in a `ParallelAgent` fan out.

agents_as_tools.description: Agents exposed to this LlmAgent as callable tools. Each is rendered as `AgentTool(<agent>)` inside `tools=[...]`. LlmAgent only; empty for every other kind.
agents_as_tools.title: Agents As Tools

description.description: Source form of `description=`. Applies to LlmAgent and the wrapper kinds (Sequential/Parallel/LoopAgent); empty for HITL and shared leaves.
description.title: Description

has_model.description: True when the source LlmAgent/HITLAgent call carries a `model=` kwarg. False means the agent has no model field defined in code. Disambiguates `model=None`, which is None both when no `model=` is present and when the model can't be mapped to a `SelectedModel` (legacy/non-conforming form).
has_model.title: Has Model

kind.description: Which ADK class the node represents.
kind.title: Kind

name.description: Agent name. For `LlmAgent` matches `LlmAgent.name`. For HITL the constant `hitl_agent`. For wrappers the wrapper's `name=` kwarg. For shared imports the imported variable name.
name.title: Name

original_name.description: The name this node carried in the source it was parsed from, when the caller kept it. Sent back on a rename so the edit can be paired with the call it came from: without it a renamed node looks like a new one, and is rebuilt instead of renamed — losing the author's formatting, their comments and the binding's place in the file. Leave unset and that older behaviour applies.
original_name.title: Original Name

read_only.description: True when the node's constructor is not one the editor can author — a user-defined `BaseAgent` subclass. It is rendered and preserved verbatim on regeneration, never rewritten.
read_only.title: Read Only

shared.description: True when the node is referenced by an imported name (e.g. `from shared import x`) rather than constructed locally. Other fields are not extractable from source for shared nodes.
shared.title: Shared

sub_agents.description: Children for wrapper kinds and LlmAgent coordinators. Always empty for HITLAgent and shared leaves.
sub_agents.title: Sub Agents

tools.description: Source form of each element in `tools=[...]` (LlmAgent only).
tools.title: Tools

FunctionNodeTemplate.description:
What to generate for a function node the diagram is creating.

Carries nothing but its kind. A function node is a step written in Python, and
what that step *does* is exactly the part a diagram cannot express — so the
template has no knobs: it produces a passthrough, and the body is the user's
to write in the Code tab.
FunctionNodeTemplate.title: FunctionNodeTemplate

eval_set.description: Generated EvalSet containing one eval case, serialized to dict. Can be passed directly to the evaluate endpoint.
eval_set.title: Eval Set

GraphNodeConfig.description:
Per-node settings adk applied, whether written by hand or defaulted.

Everything here is read-only in the diagram: it is set by decorator kwargs,
`Node` subclass fields, or adk's own wiring, none of which the plan editor
authors. Only the values actually set are persisted; the rest default here.

input_schema.description: Name of the pydantic model adk validates this node's input against. Graph validation requires the upstream output_schema to match.
input_schema.title: Input Schema

mode.description: LlmAgent mode as adk resolved it — `single_turn` for a standalone graph node, `chat` for one attached to a parent agent.
mode.title: Mode

parameter_binding.description: `state` binds the function's parameters from ctx.state, `node_input` from the node input.
parameter_binding.title: Parameter Binding

rerun_on_resume.description: Re-run the node body on resume instead of treating the resume payload as its output.
rerun_on_resume.title: Rerun On Resume

state_schema.description: Name of the schema that shadows the workflow's for this node and its descendants.
state_schema.title: State Schema

timeout.description: Seconds before the node is cancelled and raised as NodeTimeoutError. Retried like any other failure.
timeout.title: Timeout

GraphNodeConfig.title: GraphNodeConfig

provider.title: Provider

level.description: Python logging level name, case-insensitive: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. An unknown name falls back to ERROR.
level.title: Level

LoopGateTemplate.description:
What to generate for a loop the diagram is creating.

A loop in adk 2.x is a routed back-edge plus a node that emits the route,
because an `LlmAgent` cannot emit one. This describes that node — never read
from source, only sent when the diagram is asking for a loop to be built.

Nothing here is the loop's *decision*. The round cap is a safety net; ending
the loop on purpose is the agent's job, done by calling the exit tool, which
is why `allow_early_exit` exists.

allow_early_exit.description: Generate the tool an agent calls to end the loop early.
allow_early_exit.title: Allow Early Exit

loop_name.description: Names everything generated for this loop, so several loops can coexist.
loop_name.title: Loop Name

max_rounds.description: Rounds before the loop stops on its own.
max_rounds.title: Max Rounds

LoopGateTemplate.title: LoopGateTemplate

NodeLocation.description:
One place in the source that a graph node is written.

Lines are 1-based and inclusive, and span the definition as it reads — a
multi-line constructor call, a function with its decorators and body — rather
than just the line the name appears on.

kind.description: `definition` for the node itself. A generated loop gate also reports `max_rounds` (the constant holding its round cap) and `exit_tool` (the tool an agent calls to leave early), which are part of the loop without being nodes.
kind.title: Kind

NodeLocation.title: NodeLocation

exceptions.description: Names of the exception types the policy retries. `None` means every exception is retried.
exceptions.title: Exceptions

RouteNodeTemplate.description:
What to generate for a route node the diagram is creating.

Carries nothing but its kind, for the same reason the function node does: the
branch labels live on the *edges*, and the condition is the user's to write.
What this asks for is a node that emits a route at all — which is the part a
graph cannot do without.

SharedImportTemplate.description:

after which the graph refers to it like any other node. The workflow behind
it lives in its own file, so nothing about it is written here.
